items.title: US Senate Blocks Clarity Act Crypto Bill
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT) says that proposed $5,000 checks could add to the deficit and fuel inflation as he raises concerns about the plan’s price tag. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says that he expects Leon Black will be held in contempt after the House Oversight Committee panel voted to advance the matter to the full House. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Rep. Krishnamoorthi Says Leon Black Vote May Be Unanimous
items.content:
<article>Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says that he expects Leon Black will be held in contempt after the House Oversight Committee panel voted to advance the matter to the full House. Rep. Krishnamoorthi says that he expects to support the Russia sanctions bill even though it would give President Trump additional tariff authority, arguing that more pressure is needed on Russia’s oil revenues. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power."
 (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Rep. Downing Says Fed Has No Choice But To Raise Rates
items.content: <article>Rep. Troy Downing (R-MT) says that proposed $5,000 checks could add to the deficit and fuel inflation as he raises concerns about the plan’s price tag. Rep. Downing says that the Federal Reserve has “no choice” but to raise rates with inflation still above target and expects a modest increase. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Crypto’s Push Into Wall Street Suffers Setback After Bill Fails
items.author: Olga Kharif and Scott Patterson
items.content: <article>Crypto’s long march into mainstream finance took a step backward Tuesday when the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act, denying the industry a chance to turn its newfound influence in Washington into fresh rules that could outlast the current administration.</article>

items.title: Senate Advances Legislation to Regulate College Sports Landscape
items.author: Janet Lorin and Steven T. Dennis
items.content: <article>The Senate advanced a bipartisan bill that would attempt to regulate the rapidly-changing world of college sports, in a rush to move the legislation before lawmakers leave Washington for the midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Businessweek Daily: Future Proof Day Special (Podcast)
items.content:
<article>Wall Street traders refrained from making riskier bets in the countdown to the Federal Reserve decision, with stocks falling as elevated oil prices drove bond yields to multi-year highs.
Almost 350 firms in the S&P 500 dropped. Benchmark 10-year yields hit the highest level in nearly two decades. Longer-dated Treasuries extended losses after a weak $13 billion sale of 20-year bonds. Brent crude settled above $108, fueling inflation worries. Bitcoin tumbled as the US Senate blocked a landmark crypto bill in an industry loss.

On today's episode Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec host from a special episode in Huntington Beach, CA:

Tony Davidow, Senior Private Market Strategist, Franklin Templeton Institute
Jan van Eck, VanEck Funds CEO
Jaime Magyera, Senior Managing Director, Head of U.S. Wealth and Head of Retirement, BlackRock
Scott Dennis, Head of ETFs, TCW (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Rejects Trump's Midterm Mail Ballot Curbs
items.content: <article>The US Supreme Court refused to clear the Postal Service to enforce new restrictions on mail-in ballots for the congressional midterms, in a rebuff to the Trump administration. Jeff Mason has more on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Iran War Blockade Costs Strain Taiwan China Deterrence
items.author: Gerry Doyle, Becca Wasser, Jen Judson, Courtney McBride and Hayley Warren
items.content: The cost of naval operations since the buildup began in January has topped $7.1 billion — not including all the US assets being used to escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Bond Yields Surge Ahead of the Fed Rate Decision
items.content: <article>The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are DWS Group Head of Fixed Income, Americas George Catrambone, Upwork CEO Hayden Brown, Citizens Equity Research Analyst, Managing Director Jay McCanless, VSORA Chair Sandra Rivera, Rockefeller Global Family Office Private Advisor Angela Mwanza, Oaktree Portfolio Manager Danielle Poli, Wellington Management Private Capital Formation & Investor Relations Head Laura Kirk, Robinhood Futures & Prediction Markets VP & GM JB Mackenzie, MoneyGram CEO Anthony Soohoo, & Dutch Bros CEO & President Christine Barone. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Angela Mwanza Sees 25-Basis-Point Fed Cut
items.content: <article>Angela Mwanza, Managing Director and Private Advisor at Rockefeller Global Family Office, joined the program to discuss the Federal Reserve outlook ahead of tomorrow’s decision. In response to whether the Fed will act, she said she thinks the central bank is looking at a 25-basis-point move. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Bailey Lipschultz on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Sheinbaum Tax Change Eyes New Revenue But Businesses Fear Impact
items.author: Alex Vasquez and Gonzalo Soto
items.content: <article>Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is proposing sweeping changes to corporate income tax rules to raise as much as 140 billion pesos ($8.2 billion) next year, part of an effort to narrow the budget deficit but one that risks squeezing low-margin businesses.</article>

items.title: Robinhood Predictions VP on Growth in Event Contracts
items.content: <article>JB Mackenzie, Robinhood Futures & Prediction Markets VP & GM, discusses rising trading activity in prediction markets ahead of the Federal Reserve’s rate decision, with markets pricing in an roughly 85% chance of a 25-basis-point hike. He sas interest in Fed-related contracts has grown substantially over the past year, moving from relatively muted early adoption to one of Robinhood’s most popular contracts. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Leon Black Contempt Resolution Advanced by House Epstein Panel
items.author: Caitlin Reilly
items.content: <article>The House committee investigating disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein voted to recommend holding billionaire Leon Black in contempt of Congress Tuesday after he defied subpoenas for testimony and documents related to women in Epstein’s orbit.</article>

items.title: Canada Is a Sleeping Giant Economically, Says Blackstone's Gray
items.content: <article>Blackstone Inc. President Jon Gray says Canada has massive opportunities to grow due to its natural resources, looser regulatory policies and access to private capital. “Canada is a sleeping giant economically," he said Tuesday at an investment summit in Toronto. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Investors Contend With AI Alarms, Global Risk at Future Proof

<article>Paisley Nardini,  Head of Investment Strategy for Tema ETFs, discusses the industry group ETFs that are surging right now as industry leaders gather in Huntington Beach, California for Future Proof. items.title: Crypto Stocks and Tokens Drop After Senate Blocks Landmark Bill
items.author: Lydia Beyoud and Steven T. Dennis
items.content: <article>Senators from both parties blocked a landmark digital asset market structure bill in a procedural vote Tuesday, sending cryptocurrency stocks tumbling after a major setback for industry.</article>

items.title: Trump Says Kennedy Center Revamp Hinges on Adding His Name
items.author: Jeff Mason
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump threatened to scrap efforts to repair the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts unless his name is added to the building, shortly after his hand-picked board approved a renovation plan.</article>

items.title: Merz Cancels UN Trip to Address CDU Party Rebellion in Berlin
items.author: Arne Delfs
items.content: <article>Friedrich Merz cancelled his trip to the United Nations General Assembly in New York next week, changing course as the German chancellor faces growing opposition within his own conservative party ahead of closely-watched regional elections on Sunday.</article>

items.title: Brazil Top Court Puts Off Moraes Decision, Clouding Election
items.author: Daniel Carvalho, Martha Beck and Beatriz Reis
items.content: <article>Brazil’s Supreme Court delayed a decision on whether to open an unprecedented investigation into one of its justices after a tense public hearing in which members traded accusations of political bias and spreading falsehoods about each other.</article>

items.title: Hong Kong Leader to Unveil Five-Year Plan That Outlasts His Term
items.author: Nectar Gan
items.content: <article>Hong Kong leader John Lee is taking the unprecedented step of outlining a five-year vision for the Asian financial hub. The question is whether he’ll be the chief executive to see it through.</article>
